quest.title: Echoes of Fate
quest.description: To stop the Rächer of Solnari from causing further harm to Nod-Krai, you must gather all your strength and prepare for the most important battle.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1000, Primogem x30, Mora x44000, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act IV
chapter.title: An Elegy for Faded Moonlight

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Ah, Lord Sangemah Bay. How lovely to see you.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I must thank you for the device you provided, it was an enormous help. Would I be right in thinking that it was developed by the Akademiya?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Why come and ask me when you clearly know already?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I mostly came to thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Hehehe, that's more like it. A little gratitude goes a long way with Lord Sangemah Bay... Play your cards right, and you might even stand a chance of becoming my long-term supplier.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The chance to work with such a kind and charitable investor as yourself would be a great honor for the Curatorium.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Huh? Charitable? Who said anything about charity? First I'm hearing about it.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Let's see... The first plot of land you purchased in Nod-Krai, your desert interests, and—

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Pshh, tshhh, stop! What do you think you're doing, exposing my investment history!?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: It's nothing to hide from. They're all perfectly legitimate investments. And some of the land you purchased was with the intent of building a sanctuary... Yes, I heard about that too.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: How... How did you...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You're a curious case, Lord Sangemah Bay. You don't like people finding out about your good deeds, do you?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: But I'm afraid no matter how hard you try to keep things under wraps, where there's a will, there's a way.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You did it for Sumeru, didn't you?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: It was empty land that was gonna go to waste otherwise. I figured if I built something there, it might at least get some use in an emergency.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Disasters are capricious things. They strike without any warning. I've lost family to a disaster before, and I don't want to lose any friends or business partners if I can help it.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: My elder sister used to dream of finding a sanctuary. Somewhere with plenty of food, water, and medicine, where everyone could live happy lives.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: It was something I looked into. But after discussing things with the Dendro Archon, I decided on a more effective strategy.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: The tech people handled the tech, and moneybags provided the Mora. It just made the most sense.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: It's a pity that so few people know the truth about you. Everyone says that you view everything in terms of Mora, and all you care about is growing your own wealth.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: So? What's the problem with that? Everyone wants to be rich — it's human nature. So yes, I love Mora, and it's nothing to be ashamed of.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: But surely you have dreams of your own beyond just making Mora?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: You don't get it, do you? My dream is to invest in other people's dreams. And, y'know make a nice little slice for myself along the way.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Ah, just thinking about it makes me happy... that sweet, sweet sound of Mora...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: For the device?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: And the pendant.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Oh, that... I was just returning a favor. Don't worry about it.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Seems like we've both been away from home for a very long time.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Yeah... so long that I barely remember what my family even look like.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: That would be your mother, father, and sister...?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Yeah, though it's been years since my sister passed away.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: It's not like I want to forget them, obviously. But memory can be even more ruthless than the most calculating businessperson. Beyond a certain point, if something isn't helping you, it just gets rid of it.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: My sister can't help me now. Slowly but surely, her face is fading from my mind's eye. It's become a vague impression.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Not everything will fade. When loved ones pass away, the beautiful memories are the ones that last the longest.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's true. If you ask me, that's the one silver lining in all of it.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Well that, plus... I'm sure that life is much better now than it was back then?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Oh, absolutely. I have tons of Mora, a big, beautiful house, business is booming, and I'm as happy as can be!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: You've got a lot going for you, too. Boss of the Curatorium of Secrets? I'm sure there's plenty of Mora to be made in that line of work!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I appreciate the vote of confidence.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Timed that pretty well, didn't I?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You certainly did. Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It's okay. I'm just glad no one was hurt.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon noticed you doing something too, Dainsleif. Were you helping get them out?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Of course. When I asked Nefer to conduct this investigation, I was not naive to the dangers involved.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: I had a duty to ensure your safety.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Heh, good to know your sense of justice is still intact after all these years.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: I take that to mean that you saw the truth. That comes as a great relief.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I certainly did. And, thanks to your help, I also managed to trap Rerir inside the chess set.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, really? How'd you manage that?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Well, to be honest, I sensed that something was wrong long before we made it to the temple.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: By using this fragment to probe into Rerir's past... well, the monster formerly known as Rerir... it seems I alerted him. I was tracking him, then he caught on and started tracking me too. Can't say I'm surprised.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: But how did he track you through your thoughts alone? That shouldn't be possible...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Rerir was a secret agent who reported directly to the Vinster King. He is an expert at finding a trail and hunting down his pursuers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No wonder...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: He infiltrated the chess set, read my thoughts, and built a new, virtual chess set inside of it. That's why we weren't able to leave at first.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Speaking of your chess set, it's quite a remarkable item. Would I be right in thinking you have some connection to King Deshret?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You overestimate me. I only have a connection with one of his underlings, the Ibis King.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You all saw how this came to be. A long time ago, the Iab massacred my tribe, the Shimti, in our home village. A few years later, I enrolled in the Akademiya, where some new information came to light.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The Unut and the Iab fought a bitter battle over the rights to a well, all for the sake of a non-existent fifty million Mora. The Iab ultimately won that confrontation, but their victory came at the cost of almost every warrior in the tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The final blow to the Iab came at the victory feast, when an Unut assassin beheaded their chief right before my eyes. The remaining Iab fled and have been scattered to the winds ever since.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Having gotten my revenge, I returned to my hometown, where — to my surprise — the nearby temple was still standing. There it was, seemingly immune to the relentless hostility of the desert, while my tribal home lay in ruins.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: As I stood there, gazing at the temple, I noticed a cat just outside. This cat, as it turned out, was home to the spirit of the Ibis King. He led me to a gate deep inside the temple, and there he made a deal with me.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: This chess set is my gift from the Ibis King. The chessboard within is made to the same specifications as the one in the Mausoleum of King Deshret, and represents his power of piercing analysis.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: With this chessboard and its container, I gained a certain ability to perceive hidden secrets. Now, you could conclude that the Ibis King simply wanted to give the people of this world the power to seek the truth, but I don't believe that's the full story.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Every god plays favorites. Their hearts are as fickle as any human's — full of secrets, perversions, egotistical tendencies... But precious few gods are willing to admit this.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: It is the same with all powerful forces, including fate itself. Their gaze falls preferentially upon a select few. As you rightly point out, this is an act of favoritism.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: If you're alluding to the Abyss... then yes, I agree.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Gather the others. It's time to share everything I've learned.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Before long, the group is gathered in the office. Those too busy to attend inform the others of their movements...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Thank you all for being here.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: As promised, I did some further investigating into the Rächer of Solnari's background. I am pleased to report that the investigation has been most fruitful indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The Rächer of Solnari, real name Rerir, was once a Khaenri'ahn subject who served the Vinster King. I will now share the important details of his story — please save any questions or comments for the end...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Nefer narrates Rerir's backstory to the group.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: At the Vinster King's behest, he gathered intelligence and assassinated descendants of the Crimson Moon dynasty. Unwilling to take down his beloved, Tholindis, who was secretly of Crimson Moon heritage, he then got dragged into court politics...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Vedrfolnir's voice, which spoke to him of his fate, was like a reflection of the moon. Though he could disturb the waters to gain some temporary relief, he was powerless to erase it entirely.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: In contrast, Rerir's own life was like a reflection of a broken moon. Once the stormy winds of fate blew across the water's surface, it was utterly destroyed.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Tholindis smuggled away a piece of the moon before disappearing through that mysterious portal. It was passed down through the ages, finally falling into the hands of The Knave.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: But what lies on the other side of that portal? Is it really a whole other world?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Tholindis never had the chance to share what she found there. Neither did Rerir, who followed her in.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: So that's why he's so obsessed with the moon...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: A tragic tale, to be sure. But it does not excuse his many transgressions.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: No matter how much Rerir suffered in the past, the fact remains that he is what we know today as the Wild Hunt, wreaking havoc upon innocent lives in Nod-Krai.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: He becomes more dangerous with each passing day. If left unchecked, it is simply a matter of time before all of Teyvat suffers the consequences. This is a threat that the Knights of Favonius cannot ignore.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: A question for Miss Columbina. Forgive me if this is presumptuous, but have you ever seen the spatial gateway that appeared in Rerir's memory?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Never. But I have heard stories of something called the "Moon Gate," and this seems to fit the description.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Miss Lauma, any thoughts on this?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: In the lore of the Frostmoon Scions, the moon is believed to hold many secrets. Some sources speak of ancient knowledge, others of a gateway to the unknown.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: The term "moon gate" is one I have heard before. But, as is the case with all of our legends, there are no records of any firsthand witnesses. We cannot know whether it truly exists.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Then back to Miss Columbina. As a Moon Goddess yourself, do you have some idea of where the moon gate leads to?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Not at this stage, sorry. I do hold the power of the Frost Moon, and my strength is recovering well. I can sense that the gate would open at my command, but...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: But there's more to the power of the Frost Moon than that?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yes. A moon goddess has the right to open the moon gate, since it is a path to the moon. But as Nefer mentioned, holding open a spatial gateway takes a huge amount of power...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...And right now, I need to conserve my energy to fight the Rächer of Solnari. I'm afraid this is one mystery we may have to leave unsolved for now.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I agree, better to save your strength. But if you'll humor me for a moment, I have a bold conjecture of my own regarding the world beyond the gateway.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I highly suspect that neither Tholindis nor Rerir made it through unscathed. The evidence pointing to this is the fact that the Rächer of Solnari exists in the form of countless fragments.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: With the Abyssal power he wields, no ordinary foe can touch him, let alone tear him to shreds. And yet, the Wild Hunt proliferates wherever his scattered fragments lie, drawing hordes of monsters to many different locations across the land.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: So your theory is that Rerir was physically torn to shreds by some powerful force — hence why the Wild Hunt is a distributed phenomenon rather than a unified one?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Makes sense to me. Explains why the Wild Hunt is so pervasive, and why he's been trying to piece himself back together. He was whole to begin with, and he wants to be whole again.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Without the power of the Abyss on his side, he almost certainly would have perished the moment he was torn apart. But the Abyss, much like a curse, has kept him alive...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: ...I could not agree more. The power of the Abyss is most surely a curse.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It is a compelling explanation, and one that accords with my present understanding of Abyss creatures. Whether the lifeform in question is primitive or advanced, if a curse has extended its lifespan unnaturally, it will continue to survive in spite of everything.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: This raises some interesting questions... I will run some experiments and see if there is any validity to my suspicions.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: That being said, regardless of whether my research bears fruit, I would like to thank Miss Nefer for conducting such a thorough investigation. Already, it has greatly enriched my understanding of the entity we face.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: My pleasure, Mr Albedo. I, too, hope that the information I have shared today proves useful as we look to formulate the next stage of our plan.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey... What is it, Dainsleif? You look really upset...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: It's just... when I think of the man I once knew as Rerir, I struggle to understand why things had to turn out like this.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: The two of you used to be friends, didn't you? I don't know if these words will bring any comfort, but... my heart goes out to you.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Mine too.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: We can never know all the hows and whys of the way things are. The moon and stars are full of untold secrets and lies, and the skies are host to many more mysteries than these alone. Yet, none of that can begin to compare with the complexity of human life.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Those are the first comforting words I've heard in a long time. Thank you both.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Well, I think this is a good place to end today's meeting. I'm sure Nefer needs some time to recover — she's been through an awful lot today.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: That's very thoughtful of you, Lauma.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Of course.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Sounds good to me. Take some time to rest and digest before we reconvene to nail down a plan.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Hey... is this a bad time? Hope I didn't kill the conversation...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's fine! Come on in!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Haha, no need. C'mon, let's talk outside.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Mmm, nice room... Oh, I—I'm not coming in, though.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why not? It's just a hotel room...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: If it's all the same, I'll just stay out here. I might not look the part, but I am technically a knight. Barging into people's private quarters isn't the kind of thing we do...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Anyway, Nefer went back to the Curatorium to get some rest. But before she left, she shared some things with me that I thought you should be aware of.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Firstly, although she managed to trap the Rächer of Solnari inside her chess set, there's no guarantee that the power of the Ibis King is any match for one of the Five Sinners. Their powers are beyond our comprehension.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: It's only a matter of time before he finds a way to break out. We have to come up with a plan and take care of him before that happens.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Honestly, Paimon figured that might be the case... So, how long have we got?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Heh, well... I asked her that same question. She talked for a long time, but for the most part, seemed like she was trying to convince me how precious her chess set is... and what a long and storied history it has.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Felt like some kind of sales pitch. You know, the kind where you end up handing over Mora against your will? ...Anyway, after all that, she finally answered the question: Two days, at most.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Two days!? Holy moly... Can we even recruit enough help in that time?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: That remains to be seen. Which brings me to the second issue: Dainsleif is obviously conflicted about this whole thing, but given how little time we have, there's no way we can pull this off without his help.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: You have some history with him, right? Do you think maybe you could... talk to him for us?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll see what I can do.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Great. I appreciate it.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Alright, onto item three. So, Albedo, Durin, and I put our heads together and came up with a plan. Can't promise it's gonna work yet, but at least it's a start.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: We figured we'd bounce the idea off you first. We'll explore it further once everyone's recovered.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Oh? Please, ask away.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon's dying to hear this!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Alright, so... Here's what we're thinking...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: In a hushed voice, Varka lays out the current plan.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: It's a shocking plan... but nothing can faze the greatest Traveler and trustiest travel guide in Teyvat. It doesn't take you long to get behind it.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: We felt a little uneasy about roping you into this... I mean, firstly, you're not locals, and secondly, none of us are your boss. You're well within your rights to refuse, if you so choose.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Roping us in? Why would you even say that? We know the stakes here — it's all of us against the Rächer of Solnari, or none of us stand a chance.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I choose my words very intentionally, I'll have you know. I like to think there's an art to striking a down-to-earth tone even when the stakes are through the roof.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sir Varka, I have a few thoughts about this plan.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I'm all ears.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I think we can be more flexible with how the roles are allocated. In my view, the most sensible lineup would be like this...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I see your point, yeah. But if that's how we're gonna approach this... You'd better make sure you're ready.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...To be clear, I don't doubt your abilities — far from it. I just want to make sure... Are you really willing to take all this on?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I want to do everything within my power. The Rächer of Solnari is a truly fearsome opponent, and if I do my part, it'll greatly reduce the risk for everyone else involved.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Well, that tracks with what I've heard. Jean's mentioned in her letters that you're so diligent, it's almost... abnormal.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: As in, most people weigh up the risks and rewards in situations like this. But you seem to just march towards danger without a moment's hesitation.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Of course, everyone appreciates a fearless pioneer. But all that aside, I'm the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, and you're our Honorary Knight. I want to make sure your courage doesn't come at the expense of your safety.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you, Sir Varka.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I should be the one thanking you — it means a lot to have you on board. I'll give some serious thought to your suggestions.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Varka gives a very knightly bow and says he'll see you at the hotel again later. He has arranged for everyone to meet and finalize the plan of action.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: In an effort to lighten the mood, he booked out the hotel for this meeting — so you could all chat over a drink.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: ...This is a thorough plan, but I do have one last question before we take action: How can we be sure that our enemy won't leave the designated area?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Great question. Albedo's been hard at work analyzing Rerir and the Wild Hunt's behavioral patterns. His conclusions are as follows.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Firstly, from the earliest known confrontation until now, Rerir has never displayed any ability to manipulate the dimension of space. So it's unlikely he has any power in that domain.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Secondly, he seems to have a particularly strong vendetta against our group. If we put him in a fight-or-flight situation, he'll choose to fight every time.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Thirdly, finally, and most importantly: He is consumed by hatred, both for the moon, and for his enemies.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Turns out, we tick both of those boxes. We have a reincarnated moon in our ranks, and a spy who accessed his private memories without permission. He'll be baying for blood, not looking to escape.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: As someone who's had their fair share of interactions with the Wild Hunt, those all seem like valid observations to me.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Understood. Then I will defer to the verdict of the group.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Well everyone, that's the plan in full detail. Albedo and Durin are carrying out their part as we speak.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Plan approved. Scheduling...

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Okay! Any firepower you need, I got you covered. Let's light this baby up!

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: The Frostmoon Scions are behind you as well.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: And the rest of you?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...No objections? Alright, then it's settled. This is the plan we're going with. Next up, an old tradition of mine: Anyone who wants to back out, now's your chance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, we can still back out of this!?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Everyone says things they regret, right? I don't want anyone feeling trapped because their mouth said "yes" before their brain had time to think things through.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: A very "people first" approach. I hear that's common practice in the Knights of Favonius.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Heh, who'd you hear it from? Diluc?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Shh. We don't use people's real names at work. This contact will be known only as "Owl," please and thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: This plan can only work if everyone does their part. Flins and I will absolutely support it.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: We shall indeed. You'll be glad you accepted our help.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Also — you are the last person I expected to see here, Miss Dori.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Hehe, it's not often I get called Dori in a work context. My peers usually call me Lord Sangemah Bay.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Sooo... the longer your name, the higher your net worth? Is that the idea here?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Ahahaha, in that case, Mr Flins here must be worth a fortune! That's right, I know your full name. It's—

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: The walls are thin here. I'd appreciate you keeping that a secret.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Okay, okay, fine. Ugh, I'm actually only here as a favor for someone else. Do you have any idea how much it would cost to hire me otherwise!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... Does this mean someone out there actually has the power to boss Dori around?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: It most certainly does not! We have a longstanding and mutually beneficial business partnership. She's actually the mom of a friend of yours.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Said mom supplied me with a great little trinket, but now that lady's ruined everything. If I don't start building a little goodwill now, my whole business in Nod-Krai is gonna go down the drain!

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Okay, so what exactly is so special about this pendant?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: It's a lucky charm that a great mage made for me. We have a business relationship, and she was worried that something bad might happen to me. So, she wanted me to have something that can store power to protect myself with.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: I FINALLY got it all fully charged up with kuuvahki, and then Nefer went and used it all up at once! Gah, never lost so big in my life!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You're right, it was all my fault. I didn't mean to drain all the kuuvahki in the pendant, but I'll make it up to you.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: You will? Um, um, well, in that case... how about you give me your chess set and we call it even?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hehe, I knew you'd say that. Well, it's yours if you want it. In fact, take it now and I'll even throw in a free Rächer of Solnari. Deal?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Ughhh... You're putting me in a difficult position here...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: It's a very useful thing to have around... but I have a funny feeling it won't be around much longer. I guess we'll see in a couple of days.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Ugh, looks like bankruptcy for me...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Hey, don't be so pessimistic. See this through and you never know, you might find a new business opportunity on the other side.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: With an action plan in place, everyone chats among themselves before going their separate ways to get started on their work.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You and Paimon decide to check in and see how each stage of the preparations are going.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dori! How are things going, feeling ready?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Oh, I was born ready. We only have two days — you think Lord Sangemah Bay would let an opportunity like this slip by?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Don't forget, when something's in high demand, the people with the goods on hand get to charge the highest price of all! Even higher than the sellers taking advance orders.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Ta-da! See, it's right here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's so pretty! Did you make it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I had no idea you were so skilled with your hands!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Hahaha, no, I have a supplier. We go way back, so he made me a very attractive offer.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aha! No wonder you were talking about lucky charms at the meeting... You've been getting Kaveh to make them for ya!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Ehh, that's not the full story. It actually started a while back as a project between me and the Dendro Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Mage Alice once warned me that this world won't stay safe forever. There may come a day when everyone faces a great crisis.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: I passed this onto the Dendro Archon, and she secretly brought together a research team made up of Sumeru's top scholars to invent a technology that could keep people safe. I won't go into the details, because it's all very complicated — but if you wanna know more, you can ask the Dendro Archon about it some time.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Anyway, point being, it was the Dendro Archon who asked Kaveh to build this little contraption. As one of the top Kshahrewar talents, he was the obvious choice.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Took him long enough. He stressed over it for ages. Must have gone through at least a dozen designs before producing a final product... *sigh* But that's Kaveh for you.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Mehrak delivered it to me a couple of days ago, along with a letter from Kaveh... "Could I ask why I'm sending this technology to you? What's your proposed use case? Has it been approved by the relevant authorities?"

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: So nosy! Ugh, my fault for sending him the research permit to begin with!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Surely, Nahida must've told him you were involved in this project? He was probably just nervous 'cause you're always so secretive about your business.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Could be, could be. Anyway, I just replied: "Let's hope there never has to be a use case, because it would involve grave danger."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Fair enough. But it sounds like he was just being cautious. He probably felt responsible as the one who made it.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Or maybe he was asking as a favor for his housemate — he's done that before. Not sure why though. His housemate doesn't seem to really care that much about this kind of stuff.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Either way, all's well that ends well. I'm just glad to finally have my hands on the product. I wouldn't want to be without it given the potential dangers that lie ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: ...Huh? What does that look mean?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh, Paimon's just... super surprised! This must be the first time we've ever seen you actually get serious about something...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This is not the Lord Sangemah Bay we're used to...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Well, a long time ago I made a promise to myself: I promised that I was gonna live every day of my life with a big beaming smile. Obviously, Mora plays a biiiig part in that... Ahem, buuut...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: There are always gonna be times in life when you have to give something back. That could mean paying back a debt, returning a favor, or showing some kindness.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Alice has been a huge help to me over the years. She was the first investor I ever had, and I want my investors to know that Lord Sangemah Bay is the best in the business.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: And more than that, no one knows what the future will bring. Whatever happens, I want to make sure the Dendro Archon and all of Sumeru is prepared to face whatever comes.

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Oh, that? I was just making sure Nefer and I are square.

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Don't be thinking it was some sort of benevolent act. I'm no saint, so don't treat me like something I'm not.

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: My priority is doing the business that I wanna do. So long as my conscience lets me, but... it usually does. That's the Lord Sangemah Bay business model.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, if you say so.

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: I do say so, and that's the whole point. I'm a businesswoman. Don't go trying to figure out what kind of person I am, you'll exhaust yourself! Muuuch easier for everyone involved if you just take my word for it~

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Oh, and could you two help me get this stuff where it needs to be? Thanks so much! You're my favorite assistants.

choices.text: ...You never intended to ask for it back, did you?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon. Good to see you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Everything going smoothly over here?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: ...Sort of. As you're probably aware, Varka, Durin, and I captured some Abyssal creatures from the Wild Hunt.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Per the plan, we dissected and analyzed some samples of these creatures. The process went very smoothly... The findings, however, come with some troubling implications.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!? You can actually dissect the Wild Hunt?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: That depends on your definition of "Wild Hunt" and "dissection."

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Harmless... lifeless... These words are accurate descriptions.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: The Wild Hunt is an interesting phenomenon. In and of itself, it doesn't seem to possess anything akin to a human personality. But taken as a collective, the medium through which the Wild Hunt is summoned does appear to have a soul.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Master griped a lot about "The Wise" Hroptatyr, and seemed somewhat fascinated with "The Foul" Surtalogi. But she barely mentioned Rerir at all.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I don't think that was because of his lower social standing, though. Anyway, it's a pity — I should like to hear her thoughts on the nature of the lifeform he has become today.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It's a strange mix... the furious energy of an Abyssal being channeled through a fractured physical existence, a consequence of being torn apart by an unknown power...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Perhaps the only explanation for his survival in this state is that he sacrificed a degree of individuality in exchange for a continued existence...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Ahem.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Oh, sorry. Once I get talking about interesting research, I have a tendency to go on indefinitely.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Back to our research findings. Essentially, they confirm my hypothesis: Rerir's corpse is completely contaminated by the Abyss, and the effects are irreversible.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: You could think of this as Rerir in mutated form — but in my view, even that would be inaccurate. In reality, his whole being has been consumed by the Abyss. In other words, he is now nothing more than a manifestation of Abyssal power.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, at present, we have no means of completely eradicating Abyssal power. Hence, we cannot fundamentally destroy the Rächer of Solnari either.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's terrible news... So that's it, we can't defeat him? Not even if we get the power of the three moons?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Miss Columbina's situation is a difficult one. She can never achieve wholeness when the world does not accept her presence.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: It's as if her creator banished her to a place she can never be accepted... It means, she spends most of her energy just on her own survival.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Given the circumstances, it's only natural to despair. But we must see this plan through to the end.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Time to kick off the backup plan.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon almost forgot — this is for you. Dori asked us to bring it.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Ah, how wonderful. Well, thank you for making the trip. Durin and I will be heading off shortly.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I'm sorry I won't be there to protect you in person this time... Please be careful.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We will.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Alright then. Stay safe.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Miss Lauma, is everyone here?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Yes. The fate of my flock is in your hands, Grand Master Varka. Please keep them safe.

dialogues.speaker: Follower
dialogues.text: My Lady... What are you saying?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Within the next twenty-four hours, we will face the biggest crisis the world has ever seen.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: This is not a burden that we deserve to bear. But I believe that we reap what we sow in this life... So, I intend to act. I must do what I think is right.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: For me, that means fighting for the future of Nod-Krai.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: This gentleman is the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, Varka, Knight of Boreas. In my absence, please follow his lead.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Hey, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Guess I should introduce myself. Hmm... Well, to start with, I know my way around a battlefield, hahahaha.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Biggest strengths are... honesty and hardworking-ness? Anyway, point is, I don't intend to let Lauma down. I'm gonna do everything in my power to keep every last one of you safe and sound.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Something on your mind?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Miss... Columbina, was it? I believe that's how the others addressed you.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: That's right. Names are funny things... Have you always been called Dainsleif?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Yes... I take it your own name has a more complicated history?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I have a different relationship with names than other people. To be honest, I'm not even sure that "Columbina" is my name... at least, not in the same way that "Dainsleif" is yours.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: But it's what everyone calls me, and I go along with it. A lot of my life has been that way... I get so used to things that I forget to question why they are so.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I never used to think much about where names come from, or what they mean to people... Maybe something's wrong with me.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: You're different from other people. I sensed it the first time we met.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: You're more perceptive than most. I'm sure your long life and rich range of experience explains that.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Do you ever find yourself missing Khaenri'ah, Mr. Dainsleif?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Difficult to answer. I have dreamed of the past many, many times. Sometimes I'm fighting tooth and nail, other times I'm lying on the ground, defeated.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: I don't recall any happy moments from that time. It has been too long.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Is that because hatred survives longer than love and affection?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: That would not be for me to say. I make no excuses for the grudges I bear. But whatever the reason, I remember little that was beautiful or sentimental.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: ...Thank you for your help with the Rerir situation. Without your efforts, I never could have learned the hidden truth of his story.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: You're welcome. I know he's your friend.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Friend? Huh...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: He betrayed me... and I never really understood what he was going through in life... Some friendship that is.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Okay. So, do you plan to fight him with us?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: You see? You're torn. Now you know what really happened, you see the things he's done in a new light.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: I need some time.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Of course — I completely understand. Anyone else in your position would feel conflicted too.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Actually, I went through something similar myself recently. Something happened that changed my perspective on a situation. A situation I took for granted at the time, but now I feel very grateful for it.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: You mean the Harbingers who still support you, even though you've left the Fatui.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yes.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I always thought they were only helping me because Harbingers are forced to work together. But then I abandoned them. A warrant was even put out for my arrest...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yet even now, they support me. Which means, I was wrong about them all along.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Clearly, they view you as a friend.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I feel a little guilty now. I regret not seeing their help for what it was... and not treasuring it.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I see the guilt that you're feeling now, because I feel it too. Hopefully, talking about it will do us both some good.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: #...Have you noticed that {NICKNAME} and Paimon are over there? I think they've been listening.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Huh. Shall we say hello?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Sure.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hello.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aah! They caught us!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sorry... We were just concerned about you...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: I apologize for making you worry.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: No doubt you wish to know where I stand on the plan to take down Rer... the Rächer of Solnari. I'm afraid I need a little time. But I will seriously consider joining you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You will? Thank you so much! Everyone will be so grateful to hear that.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: They needn't be. This was something that I was going to have to face up to eventually.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: That doesn't matter to them. They're grateful to you regardless.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: You can't control their gratitude, so just accept it. And then, have a think about whether you're willing to join us.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Ah. You're earlier than I expected.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Flins. Been waiting here long?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Not too long. I came a little early so I'd have some time to think.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you nervous about the battle?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Quite the opposite... I'm reminiscing on my past battles.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: When I was awakened by the Ratniki, I had not touched a weapon in many years. I felt like the battlefield was not where I belonged.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: But after waging war against the Wild Hunt for so long, I came to realize something... A life of absolute peace is simply not a possibility for me.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: My restless flame indicates that somewhere inside of me, there is a deep yearning to root out the evil in this world.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That doesn't sound like such a bad thing...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I agree.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Well, in the past, when I was a fae whose primary concern was hibernation, it was hardly ideal.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: But it certainly serves me well here in the present. And I am delighted to be able to join forces with you in this endeavor.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Looks like I'm not the first to arrive.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Ah, Miss Lauma.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did you sleep okay last night?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I struggled to settle down at first because of the nerves... But don't worry — I got enough sleep in the end. I'll be just fine.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks for everything.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Please. I'm just doing my part.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nefer! Over here!

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Aino asked me to relay a message. She said, Ineffa will be on high alert and keep a close watch over all secondary districts where defense is required, providing support as necessary.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Meanwhile, Aino herself will provide ranged support to us directly, using her latest invention.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Excellent. My thanks to all involved.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... The chess set's looking a little unstable...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: It won't hold him much longer. We should be prepared to engage at a moment's notice.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: No sense sitting around waiting. Let's make the first move while we still have the option.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: I agree. Paimon, find a safe hiding place.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #G—Got it. Uhhh... be careful, {NICKNAME}!!!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I will.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Everyone, take your positions as soon as the battle starts.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Every ounce of strength we have in our bones, let us bring to this fight.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Ready?

response.speaker: Everyone
response.text: Let's go.

response.speaker: Everyone
response.text: Let's go.

response.speaker: Everyone
response.text: Let's go.

response.speaker: Everyone
response.text: Let's go.

response.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
response.text: Hah, I've seen all your futile ploys before. You have become the authors of your own demise.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: I wouldn't be so sure about that.

response.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
response.text: You are merely a moment of sport before I tear down the moon.

choices.text: And the backup plan is underway.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...That's the only reason you're here?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yes. I've thought a lot about it, and I've realized that you, me, and Arlecchino should be friends.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I think this is very important, so I felt I had to come and tell you.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Well, this is a new one. I'm so moved, I can't even hold my teacup... If that's all, you can leave now.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Do you not want to be friends with me? Or is it that you prefer being coworkers?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: What is this, Columbina? Are you deliberately testing my patience threshold? Right now, my politeness module is active, but if you say another word, I swear I'll shut it down!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...If your politeness module was active, wouldn't you say the word "please" at some point?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Pulonia, please see Lady Columbina to the door.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Will you still invite me to your next tea party?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...What?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Yes, I think you will. Bye-bye, dear Sandrone.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Last time, the Wild Hunt escorted you out. Would you rather I handled it myself this time?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We just wanted to... y'know, see how you were doing now that it's all over...

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Why? Out of concern for my safety? Hah. I hope you didn't seriously think that the Rächer of Solnari would be able to lay so much as a finger upon me, given how prepared I was.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mostly 'cause you kinda helped us out, so we just wanted to check you were okay. Looks like all your robots are fixed, huh?

choices.text: I spy books and teacups on the table...

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Oh, don't you worry about that, teatime is already a write-off. The visitor before you managed to kill my appetite.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: If you're in the mood for tea, go ahead and help yourself. Otherwise, it's going to waste.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: My coasters are still missing in action, though. Use this notebook instead.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, pretty hefty notebook... Look at all those calculations...

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: You can ignore those. They're just dumb scribblings.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: I doodle and write in my free time. Sometimes, I remember the distant, dreamlike past, sometimes, I imagine the far-flung future.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: And other times, I grit my teeth and note down all the crazy nonsense going on in the present. Some people do the crosswords in the newspaper — this is my equivalent of that.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Trying to predict the future is like daydreaming, and writing about the present just makes me furious. The past is my favorite. If nothing else, it's already set in stone, so I don't have to rack my brains trying to figure it all out.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Huh... Although, having said that, the only vaguely interesting memory in my past is probably that guy they call Lord-Artificer.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Who else? Pretty much all the meka in Fontaine are his personal handiwork.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, are you saying you know him? Like, personally? As a friend?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Umm... I mean, I guess we were friendly enough.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Yup. In fact, I'm probably the only "normal" person left who knew him at all.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: We used to chat occasionally back when he was still around. Before he passed away, he asked me to destroy all his manuscripts.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: I honored his request. But, I did read through everything first before destroying them.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: I mean, I couldn't let the genius of Lord-Artificer Alain Guillotin disappear like that. Would have been such a waste.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... that's where the formulas in your notebook are from...?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: I just told you, those are my equivalent of crossword puzzles. They're just dumb formulas that I solve for fun when I'm bored.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Alain's work was like epic poetry. The formulas in my notebook are just silly little riddles in comparison.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Not that there's anything bad about them. I mean, at least... solving those riddles isn't going to hurt anyone. Except me, 'cause I lose a few brain cells in the process.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Anyway, while we're on the topic, I might as well tell you about what happened to him and his friends.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Alain Guillotin had two close buddies, Rene and Jakob. They spent their childhood years together in the Narzissenkreuz Institute.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: They were all quite competitive, so there was some rivalry between them, but it was a friendly rivalry.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: But beneath the friendship and the rivalry ran something deeper: a sense of nostalgia for the past.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Unfortunately, childhood would end, the prophecy would come true, the apocalypse would arrive, and the future would never be.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: A mad dream, that would normally only capture the minds of lunatics, began to take root in their hearts: A dream of saving the world...

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: ...And if Rene and Alain had been people of lesser wits, that dream would probably have ended up as something for them to joke about in their older years.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: But alas, they were some of the sharpest minds around. They nurtured that dream with the full power of their intellect, and it grew into something that ate away at their souls.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: The first of them to fall under its spell was Rene.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Against Alain's wishes, he persisted in experimenting on a mutual friend of theirs to try and save their life. Alain did not approve, and parted ways with Rene.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: It's complicated... Alain wanted to believe that Rene only did what he did for the sake of their friendship. But when he told me about what happened, I could tell that he still had some suspicions about Rene's motives.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: ...Perhaps the seed that would grow into a nightmare had already sprouted in Rene's mind, even then.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: The next time they met, Rene's soul had been completely engulfed by the dream of salvation. His futile attempt to change the tide of fate only resulted in a wave that swallowed up the world even before the apocalypse came.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: And although that wave died down eventually, I hear that it just recently came back with a vengeance.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: As I understand, Rene wanted to live out his dream of salvation once more.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: But I'm told that the attempted resurgence finally died out for good. At long last, Rene awoke from his deluded dream... Though of course, by then, it was far too late.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, what do you think of Rene?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Do you admire his transcendent genius? His view that any price was worth paying to achieve the lofty goal of saving the world?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Or do you despise him? Dismiss him as an evil madman, who wrought havoc on the lives of everyone around him as he pursued his delusional dream?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Hmph, same difference, really. Just a matter of perspective.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Doesn't surprise me. You share one thing in common, after all. You both want to be the savior.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: The only difference is, your dream came true, and his... well, he wasn't the one who made it come true.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What about you? What's your take on Rene?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: I don't like fanatics who give up their whole lives for their ideology. Nor do I like fools who let their delusions take control.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Maybe I could understand if Rene had just been an ordinary person... but he had a sage-like intellect, and still managed to get himself lost in the labyrinth of his own desires...

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Anyway, that's enough about Rene. Now, moving on to Alain Guillotin, the Lord-Artificer.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: He managed to put a stop to the first storm whipped up by Rene. But after that, Alain lost his friends and family.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: To his credit, I suppose, the loss of his family and friends was purely a tragic accident. It's not like Alain sacrificed them for his cause, or anything.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: After that, the only thing supporting his work was the same dream that had dragged his closest friend down to the Abyss.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: But although the desire to save Fontaine drove him to found the Fontaine Research Institute, Alain continued to reject any form of transcendental knowledge or power. He was suspicious and fearful of it, having seen the way it had affected his closest friend.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: I think that formulas and machines derived solely from human intellect were the only thing that gave him a sense of spiritual comfort.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Yet Alain's intellect was simply too great. It barely left him space to breathe in his lifetime.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Once he realized that the end of his life was approaching, he finally accepted the truth: The Narzissenkreuz Institute needed someone, and a human being, to see its story through to the end.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: He quit working on his formulas, trading them in for the fairytales that had played such a formative role in his childhood, but which he'd barely touched in his adult life.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: He told me that the director of the Narzissenkreuz Institute used to read those fairytales to the children as bedtime stories. Apparently, they worked wonders at sending kids off to sleep.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: I think that all he wanted at that time in his life was to be able to sleep deeply without being plagued by depression. By that point, nothing else really mattered.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: At the very end, he laid down to rest in the ruins of the former Narzissenkreuz Institute orphanage, while the Fontaine Research Institute he had founded continued tirelessly with its work.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Many years after that, tensions over competing dreams would once again cause a rift, this time between members of the Fontaine Research Institute... but the actions of those fools had nothing at all to do with Alain.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: And that is the story of two people from the Narzissenkreuz Institute who both wanted to save the world.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: One went all in on his fantasy of salvation without ever looking back, and ended up calmly sinking to the bottom of the deepest sea.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: The other sought desperately to burn bright in his life, even though he wasn't sure where he was going.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Hmph... I do sometimes wonder, why is it that people like them have such grand hopes of saving the world?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Even the grandest tree starts as a tiny seed. So perhaps, for each of them, their mission to save the world began with a very simple desire: to save themselves.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: They were young children with friends and family who mattered to them, desires to explore the meaning of life, ambitions to have a successful career... They didn't want to see all of that taken away in one fell swoop.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Or maybe they just wanted to find something to anchor themselves within the chaos, to stop them getting quietly swept away by the storms of life.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: But instead, the search for their own salvation took them down the rocky road laid out by fate.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, do you think the desire to save oneself is enough of a justification to try and save the world?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: The way you said that sounded just like Alain... I asked him the same question back when he was in his prime, putting all of his energy into his work.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: He gave the exact same answer as you did.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: No elaboration, just a quick, short answer before getting right back to his work. He was always that way.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Alain was much more straightforward about it. I asked him the same question back when he was in his prime, putting all of his energy into his work.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Yes. It's enough.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: That was all he said before getting right back to his work. He was always that way.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Alright, teatime's over.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: I owe Arlecchino a favor for telling me these stories. I'll have to bring a whole sack of gifts the next time I visit the House of the Hearth.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: I'm gonna go tinker with Pulonia now. You guys can do whatever you want, as long as it doesn't involve interrupting me.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Pulonia, exit hibernation mode. Begin diagnostics.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Sensible answer. Glad to know you've got your head screwed on straight.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Alain would disagree, though. I asked him the same question back when he was in his prime, putting all of his energy into his work.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: "Yes. It's enough."

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: No elaboration, just a quick, short answer before getting right back to his work. He was always that way.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: You don't know...? Huh. I guess that's a fair answer. At least you're not trying to hide your confusion.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Really? Hmm. I can't tell whether that's because you disapprove of his deeds, or because he failed... or maybe you have some other reason.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Rene no longer exists in this world, and the dream he started went on to be realized by someone else.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: What a cop-out. But I suspect you'd have a more incisive and insightful answer if we dug into it further.

choices.text: But he lived hundreds of years ago...
Afternoon tea. So we are interrupting, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: How've you been holding up? Any adverse reactions? If you start to take a turn for the worse, make sure you tell me right away.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: You don't need to worry about me, Grand Master. I'm fine. I mean, I barely did anything, so...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: What? Hahaha, you're too humble, young man.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: You played an indispensable role in the battle for Nod-Krai. We can't thank you enough for your support.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Sometimes, when people praise you, it's because you deserve it. The best thing is to accept it calmly and with grace. It's important to learn how to respond to words of admiration.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Let's do a quick demonstration: "Albedo, that was an incredible feat of alchemy! The pressure was on, but you worked flawlessly at lightning speed to get the job done!"

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Thank you. I can't take all the credit, though — Durin played a big part in forming the alchemical array.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: See? Did you catch that? A masterclass in how to take a compliment.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Umm... Okay, yeah, I did work pretty hard to help prepare for the battle. No point denying that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, you guys!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Seriously, great work everyone. You all outdid yourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: #Hey, look who's bounced back! Looking good, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Seems like you've recovered. You won't need to take any more medication.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Can I get you a drink?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You know how to order at a bar now? You've sure learned a lot recently!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Handling a drinks order is ridiculously simple compared to alchemy. Don't worry, I'll blend into society yet.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon believes it! You're clearly a fast learner, just like your brother.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: To be totally honest though, Paimon didn't quite follow all the details when you first explained the plan to us... Hehe...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Don't worry, that's completely understandable. Unless you're a student of alchemy, it's hard to grasp the principle and how the process works.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: To put it in the simplest terms, we saw how our enemy stole the power of kuuvahki, and that gave us the idea of stealing his power to turn it against him.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: When facing an enemy you have no hope of defeating, it's best not to engage them in battle.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: So, instead of looking for a way to overpower him, we decided to help Columbina get strong enough to at least stand up to him in a fight.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: For this to work, we had to analyze his modes of attack, confirm who his main target was, and make sure that he wouldn't go beyond the range of the alchemical array.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: For added security, we prepared a total of four arrays, but to mitigate the impact of the battle, we identified one location in particular as the ideal spot, which is where the confrontation took place.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: The alchemical array absorbed his Abyssal power, then Durin processed it to render it usable by Columbina.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: That power enabled her to do what would otherwise have been nigh on impossible.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: What surprised me was that Dainsleif actually agreed to join us.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Given his history with Rerir, he had every right to sit this one out... But we're extremely grateful for the decision he made.

choices.text: Confronting a former friend in battle...

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: It must have been a painful choice to make. But I'm sure that making a decision was far better for him than staying in limbo.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Absolutely.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: He was torn between two paths, but in the end, he made his choice and stuck to it resolutely. He doesn't strike me as the sort of person who'd stay trapped in limbo for long.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Anyway, however you cut it, everyone gave a stellar performance! And now it's time to kick back and celebrate!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: *panting*...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nefer, how are your eyes?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: They're fine. Apart from the blindness, of course.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It's not too late.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Let me handle it.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Miss Nefer... It's not like you to lose your composure. That was the most reckless thing I've ever seen you do.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Reckless how? The situation was critical. Our lives were at stake. We had to do something.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Even so...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: *sigh* Okay, I guess you're right. Under the circumstances, it was a wise decision. You traded your eyes for an incredible victory.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: In business terms, I suppose that's a huge return on investment.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I'd be hard-pressed to argue otherwise.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Still, I don't like this outcome. And I don't want you to lose your sight for good.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: People suffer when they make sacrifices they shouldn't have to make. Whether that means faith, strength... or in this case, your ability to even see.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I had hoped you could win without sacrificing so much as a single hair on your head.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Thank you. Really.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: All done.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Don't try and open your eyes just yet. We'll see how you're doing in a couple of days. Until then, please follow your recovery plan to the letter.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I'll send full details through Jahoda. For now, just get yourself home, relax, and rest.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: My dear friends, we have fought bravely and achieved a spectacular victory. A dark cloud has been lifted from the skies of Nod-Krai... All in this land will be grateful for what you have done.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The moon will remember this day. Thank you both.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Jahoda shows up and helps Nefer get home. And you, of course, have Paimon to escort you back.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The sight of Nefer navigating the road with her eyes closed is a new one for you. She proceeds cautiously, but as her silhouette disappears into the distance, you notice she seems almost smug.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: There's something I want to let you know.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: When Durin connected everyone's minds so I could access their powers, I also felt everything they felt.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: And since Nefer's eyes were injured, my eyes are hurting now, too...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Huh? Hold on, let me try—

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I only feel the pain, there's no actual damage. I just thought I should tell you.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: ...Huh. You're right, there's no damage. That's a relief.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: But I must say, I'm surprised to hear the Kuutar share something like this with me. In the past, you never used to open up about yourself.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Things are a little different now from how they were. I'm learning to share how I truly feel with my friends.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Friends... You have no idea how glad I am to hear that.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You can't help but break into a smile at the word "friends," as a warm and fuzzy feeling fills your chest.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: One by one, your fellow teammates report in to inform you that everything is under control. At Lauma's insistence, you lie down. You fought on the front line against Rerir, and now you need rest.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nefer! Your eyes are bleeding!

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Hah. Soon, you will be powerless to resist.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: And then, I will reduce you to dust.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: But that dust will plague your memories.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Come on, keep holding on...)

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Any other tricks up your sleeve? Let's see them.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: As entertaining as they are... You've backed yourself into a corner.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You don't fool me. I see your fear, clear as day.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (I have to stoke his rage! Make him unleash everything!)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You fear what you could never defeat. You fear the thought of never being able to save your beloved.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You cannot win the fight against fate, Rerir.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Hmph. Is that what you think?

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Well, now it's your turn to feel afraid.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: The only way to defeat Rerir is to borrow his own power.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: That means Columbina will have to disappear while you two bear the brunt of his attacks.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: You have to hold on. Find a way to keep him focused on killing the two of you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yay, you're awake!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How you feeling? Any aches and pains? Did you sleep well?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm doing alright, Paimon. No need to worry about me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, well that's good... Paimon's been sitting on the edge of the bed worrying about you for ages! You slept a whole day and night... Poor Paimon had to eat all by her lonesome...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Glad to hear you didn't starve. How was the food?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, it wasn't the same without you there to share it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh* Honestly, Paimon just can't relax when you're not your usual self. She couldn't enjoy the food and settle down to sleep.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, I'm back to normal now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh yeah, and Albedo swung by earlier. He said to tell you to head to the tavern when you woke up. Varka and the others are organizing a victory feast, and they wanna celebrate with you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He also dropped off some medical supplies, but you seem fit as a fiddle, so... hehe, guess you won't be needing those.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If you're feeling up to it, let's head over now! Wouldn't wanna keep them waiting!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *fanfare* We're heeeeere!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} and Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Perfect timing! We were literally just saying how there's no way we're holding this victory feast without you. Any longer, and we would've postponed it till tomorrow!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: How are you feeling today?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Much better, thanks. Don't worry about me.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
