dialogues.text: Relieved to hear it. If that changes, just let me know. Happy to check you over at any time.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Yep. We're here for you. Anything you need, just let us know.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh wait, where's Nefer?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How are her eyes doing?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Nefer's right over there.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I'm sure she'd love to catch up with you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nefer!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon. Are you recovering well?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Much better, thanks to a good rest. You're looking well too.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Turns out that Moonchanter has some real talent, after all. My eyes were mostly recovered after just a couple days' rest. I can actually open them again now.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Yeah, but you gotta be careful... Lauma says not to strain your eyes while they're still healing.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Yes, thank you, I'm well aware.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Jahoda, could I borrow you for a moment? I could do with an extra pair of hands.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Oh, sure! Coming!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Did you hear that? I gotta go help Lauma for a second — you guys chat among yourselves. I'll grab us some drinks on the way back. Paimon, you still like 'em sweet?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You bet! Hehe, make it extra sweet, 'cause Paimon's earned it!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Sure thing!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's on your mind?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...The Rächer of Solnari. Kind of a snake, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hmm... More of a wolf in my mind.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: No, definitely a snake. A poisonous one, who spewed his venomous hatred everywhere.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Anyone who seeks revenge out of hatred for other people has become a snake. That's something my dad used to say.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I guess he didn't like seeing people go down the path of vengeance.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Perhaps. I'm sure it sounds like a very wise and open-hearted perspective to your ears. But me? I think hatred is a perfectly justifiable emotion.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: What else is left when everything you depended on in life gets stripped away? Something's gotta fuel that drive to keep on living.

choices.text: When I look at your life...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: If you're worried about me, you can nip that in the bud. I'm not someone who gets stuck in the past.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: It's just... I suddenly feel like I was wrong to call my father a liar. He was just a fool. That's why the Akademiya turned their back on him, and why the other tribes ganged up on him.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Oh, father... How much better things could have been if you were a skilled liar....

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Look at the Ibis King... Thoth is a fiendishly cunning liar. And yet, strangely, he feels more like a father to me than my real dad ever was.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: He's never brought it up, but I'd bet he feels the same way.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Why else would he give me the power to perceive the truth, while at the same time training me in the art of deception?

choices.text: Sadly, I've never heard the Ibis King's voice...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Well, King Deshret banished him to Aaru, which is essentially a prison, and posed three questions to him. He promised that he'd have his freedom if he could find the answers.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: His response was to take on a physical form and approach me, hoping that I could become his envoy and search for one of the answers on his behalf.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Did he really think I'd fall for that? He's stuck there. He can't make me return what he gave to me.

choices.text: Sounds like he was nice enough to you.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: So that's enough for you to decide he's nice, is it?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: He's a prisoner, and he was scared. So he decided to perform some good deeds to win people's approval.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: He lives in fear because he's a deceiver. How is Rerir any different? You can't work as a spy your whole life and expect a happy ending.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: It's preposterous, yet I can't say I don't understand it. Liars live in the darkness of their own making, but it's still human nature to want to go on living.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: ...They say that a liar's soul is the most worthless thing in the world. What do you think?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Good. If you understand that, it means you're smart. And you see things objectively.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: If you ask me, the soul of a liar really is worth nothing. Because all they care about is themselves.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: For example, when something good falls into my lap, I don't go sharing the news around. Stops other people trying to steal it from me.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: ...Pfft.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I have a feeling some people over there may have overheard that...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: So be it. They have sharp ears... I can't keep anything from them.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is that your way of saying you've warmed up to them now?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Oh, is that what it looks like?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What it looks like is, you're starting to see us as your friends.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Well... You all know my past now, and I can't simply eliminate everyone who knows too much. So, I guess I just have to put up with you — for the foreseeable future, at least.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: When you find yourself in a situation you can't control, the safest play is to keep calm and start monitoring everyone involved like a hawk. In the intelligence world, you need to have a sense of perspective and play your hand accordingly.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: If you understand what's at stake, please ensure my secret is safe with you. I trust you'll respect my wishes as a friend... but don't forget, I will also be watching you like a hawk.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Very good.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, wait! Now that the panic's over and we've all calmed down, Paimon's suddenly remembered something!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What is it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: After all that build up, our mystery ally never showed up even once!

response.speaker: Sound
response.text: (A noise is coming from indoors)

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: ...Huh?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: ...Am I imagining things?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Oh, really? Well, it takes a very kind person to find compassion even for liars.

choices.text: You definitely sound like father and daughter...
I see a lot of things that you can depend on.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: So, that "close colleague" who stayed behind with you... What's he been up to recently?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Don't know, don't care. I get more normal human interaction from hanging out with B.O.S.C.O. 2 than him.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Although, now you mention it, he hasn't bothered me in a while. I wonder if...

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: If he's disappeared without a trace, it's the biggest gift he ever gave to the world. But I somehow doubt that's what's going on.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: He won't lie low forever... so we'd better stay on guard.

talks.objective: Listen to what everyone is talking about
Listen to what everyone is talking about

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: I see you've recovered?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #You bet! Snoozed {M#his}{F#her} way to a full recovery...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm doing much better. Thanks for checking on me.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Glad to hear it.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: A healthy body is paramount — nothing else in life is possible without it. So take it slow. You can't afford an injury.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm so grateful that you decided to help us in the end.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon too! You really saved the day when you swooped in to open that gateway!

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: I came to accept that although Rerir was my friend in the past, here and now, he was an enemy that must be defeated.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Though I will never fully understand what happened between us, I could not let this crisis deepen any further.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: We fought a very necessary battle. And you played your part admirably.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you. I know it was hard, but you'll get through this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! And if you ever need to talk, just remember, we're always here!

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: I'll do that.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Hello you. Recovered from the battle?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Mostly recovered, thanks. I'm touched that you'd ask.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Come on, what do you mean? Of course I'm gonna ask! I care about my friends' wellbeing. And we are friends, aren't we?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Get yourself a drink, you've more than earned it! In fact, today, your drinks are on me. Lord Sangemah Bay's got you covered!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, really? What about Paimon, has she earned it, too? Has she, pleeease?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: #Hmm... Well, you haven't been through quite as much as {NICKNAME}, but... Ah, what the heck! Sure!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yay! Wow, drinks on Dori — what a historic day!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Hey! Keep your voice down, or everyone else is gonna want in, too!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: You, you... Have you heard anything I've been saying recently!? Doing business in Nod-Krai has been an absolute nightmare! If I'm buying for everyone, I'll—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, okay, Paimon will speak more quietly. Geez...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: That's more like it.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Don't you forget, Lord Sangemah Bay doesn't just go around buying drinks for anyone and everyone...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I thought of a thousand ways to congratulate you, but... now you're here, words are failing me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehehe, the Honorary Knight stuns them speechless once again!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Hahaha, well said. The Honorary Knight showed us all how it's done.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: The other knights tell me that Mondstadt was the first stop on your journey. All of us are truly delighted to count you as our friend.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I'd like to thank you for supporting the Knights of Favonius, and also for helping us save Nod-Krai.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't mention it, Grand Master.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Nonsense! Of course I'm gonna mention it! This is more than just business — it's a relationship. And there can be no relationship without showing gratitude where it's due.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Back at the hotel, you sit with Paimon for a while and discuss what lies ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Before long, Varka comes knocking...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's nearly showtime... Let's go rendezvous with the others. You know the place!
